steps: Assemble before installing

The flue collar ships in the top position, with the front ash lip and combustor monitor inside the stove. Switch the collar to rear exit if needed, take out the ash lip, and install accessories before the stove goes into its final position.

1. Rear exit: hold the M6 flange nuts inside the flue collar so they don't fall into the stove, remove the two M6 bolts and M6 fender washers with a 10 mm open end or socket wrench, turn the collar to the rear and re-attach it with the same hardware.
  2. Take out the front ash lip; it sits loosely on top of the base plate inside the burn chamber.
  3. Install accessories before locating the stove in its final position, using the instructions supplied with each kit.

Blower Kit 156431 (thermostatically controlled, 120 cfm) mounts on the back of the stove and must be installed with Rear Heat Shield 154332, which is not included in the blower kit. Combustor monitor installation is in section 5.5.
Chimney connector

6" (152mm) single-wall pipe, 24 gauge black steel minimum, never aluminum or galvanized. Crimped end toward the stove, three sheet metal screws per joint, no more than two 90° elbows, 36" (915mm) max. horizontal run sloping up 1/4" per foot.

• Attach to the flue collar with the 2 self-drilling screws in the miscellaneous kit.
  • Keep it short and direct; recommended total stove pipe length not over 10 feet.
  • Don't use connector pipe as a chimney.
  • No part may pass through an attic or roof space, closet or other concealed space, or through a floor or ceiling. All sections must be accessible for cleaning.
  • Combustible wall or partition pass-throughs must conform with NFPA 211.
  • Don't connect to a chimney flue servicing another appliance.
Qualify the chimney

Use a code-approved masonry chimney with flue liner, or a prefabricated UL 103 Type HT (2100°F) chimney. An existing chimney must pass a UL 1482 Level II inspection; the flue must be no smaller than the flue collar's cross-section and no more than three times larger.

• Masonry flue: no more than two times the flue collar area if one or more walls are exposed to the outside below the roof line; reline larger flues with a listed or code approved liner.
  • Fireclay liner at least 5/8" thick, set in refractory mortar, with at least 1/4" air space to the chimney wall; nominal 8" X 8", not larger than 8" X 12"; round liners 6" to 8" inside diameter.
  • Brick or modular block wall 4" nominal minimum; mountain or rubble stone at least 12".
  • No other appliance in the same flue; airtight clean-out door at the base.
  • Prefab: listed to UL 103 HT; follow the maker's instructions and clearances (usually a minimum of 2").
Chimney height
Minimum 15 feet (4.57 m), at least 3 feet above the highest point where it passes through the roof and 2 feet above any part of the roof or structure within 10 feet horizontally (fig. 3).

Short or exterior masonry chimneys may struggle to build draft; excessive draft causes high stove temperatures and short burn times and can be corrected with a butterfly damper. Target draft is .05 - .10 w.c. (p. 11).

The 15 foot figure is the minimum; the manual also notes that chimneys shorter than 14 feet may not provide adequate draft, which can spill smoke into the room when loading the stove or with the door open (p. 5).
Connect to the chimney

Masonry thimble: lined with ceramic tile or metal and cemented in; the connector slides fully in to the liner's inner surface without protruding, sealed with refractory cement. Prefab chimney: use the maker's adapter, fastened with three sheet metal screws.

Wall pass-through (NFPA 211 common method)

  • Remove all combustibles at least 12" around the connector; with a 6" round liner that's 31" x 31".
  • Fill with at least 12" of solid brick (3 1/4" thick, 4" nominal) around an ASTM C35 fireclay liner with a 5/8" minimum wall; refractory mortar at the chimney junction.
  • Locate it at least 18" from the ceiling.

Hearthmount into a masonry fireplace

  • Rear exit flue collar height: 28 1/4" (718 mm) on standard legs, 26" (660 mm) on short legs.
  • Seal the flue off from room air (NFPA 211 12.4.5.1): a fixed steel plate in place of the damper, or a non-combustible plate at the fireplace opening, sealed with high-temperature sealant; or a full listed liner to a sealed chimney cap.
  • Meet the trim and mantel clearances (pp. 22-23) and floor protection (p. 7).
Not to be installed in any factory built fireplace.
Floor protection & bottom heat shield

Install the supplied bottom heat shield, then continuous, sealed non-combustible floor protection: 50.25" wide x 40.75" deep minimum in the US, 52.25" wide x 48.75" deep in Canada. Only concrete over earth is exempt.

Bottom heat shield (fig. 16, p. 19)

  1. Bend the flattened heat shield on the perforations, painted side down.
  2. Use a 10 mm wrench to remove the two bolts from the bottom of the ash compartment.
  3. Oriented as shown, use the two bolts to attach the heat shield to the stove bottom.

Floor protector

US: at least 16 in. forward of the door opening, 8 in. from the sides of the door opening, 2 in. under the connector. Canada: 18" from the front, 8 in. from the sides and rear, 2 in. under the connector. Mortar or seal the sections together and remove any carpet underneath.
Set clearances

Use the clearance table and diagrams on pp. 22-23: unprotected walls with single-wall pipe and no heatshields need 14" side, 18" rear, 13" corner, and the left side load door needs 36" to combustibles. No heat shield other than Rear Heatshield Kit #154332 may be used.

• Listed pipe shields must start 1" above the lowest exposed point of the connector and extend at least 25" above the top of the stove; listed double wall pipe is an acceptable alternative.
  • Wall-mounted protection per NFPA 211.
  • The left side load door may not be used in alcove and corner installations; it must be locked with the Side Door Lock Kit.
Alcove or mobile home

Alcove: listed double-wall pipe, bottom heatshield, Rear Heat Shield #154332 if unprotected, R-value 1.6 hearth, side door locked. Mobile home: Floor Mounting Kit #750304, Outside Air Kit #154335, chimney attached directly to the stove and at least 3 ft. above the roof.

Full alcove and mobile home conditions are in the "Alcove & mobile home" spec card. Do not install the stove in a bedroom or sleeping area (mobile home section).

The alcove side door lock is Side Door Lock Kit #155850 (pp. 7, 8, 15, 17, 22 and 23); the manual also prints the number once as 155840 (p. 8).
Install the combustor monitor

Remove the lower set screw on the right side panel with a 3mm hex key (never the upper one; it secures the top plate), reorient the thermometer's magnet (figs. 13c-13e), and insert the probe fully so the magnet holds to the cast iron side plate.
Break-in fires
Before any hot fire, burn three gradual fires: monitor to 200°F for about 1 hour, then the stove to 400°F max. for 1 hour, then a 500°F surface temperature, cooling to room temperature after each.

items: Weak or erratic draft → backpuffing: smoke leaks through the stove or connector joints
Chimney too short → smoke spills when loading or with the door open; back puffing
Short exterior masonry chimney → hard to reach and hold draft temperatures
Exhaust fan or clothes dryer → low room pressure, flow reversal; Outside Air Kit #154335 may help
Unseasoned wood → weak draft and creosote

Door(s) left partially open or ash door open → over-firing
Excessive draft → high stove temperatures, short burn times; butterfly damper

fire.title: Starting a fire
fire.html:
Burn only solid, natural wood. Build the fire on the bottom of the firebox and never raise it up. Keep the ash door shut whenever the stove is burning.

Traditional fire

  1. Slide the air lever fully right (open). Put several sheets of crumpled newspaper on the grate, then small dry kindling (about 1" thick) topped with two or three small logs (about 3" to 5" thick).
  2. Light it and close the door. Build the fire slowly with larger and larger logs.
  3. Once the stove reaches 500° to 600°, set the air lever for the heat and burn time you want.

Top-down fire

Less smoke at start-up, and the chimney starts drawing sooner.

  1. With the air lever fully right, lay two short quarter-split logs on the firebox floor, about 6 inches apart, running front to back.
  2. Lay kindling across them, then one or two smaller logs on top.
  3. Tuck newspaper between the two bottom logs, under the kindling. Light it and close the door.
  4. Add kindling and small logs as needed. Keep the air fully open until the fire is well established.
New stove? Do the break-in fires before you build a hot one.
Note: The safety notices say not to use a grate and to build the fire directly on the hearth (p. 3); the fire-starting section says to burn wood directly on the stove's bottom grate (p. 11).

breakin.title: Breaking in a new stove
breakin.html:
Cast iron expands and contracts as it heats and cools, so a new stove needs a short series of small-to-medium fires before its first hot one.

  1. Open the air lever fully. Light a small fire of newspaper and kindling and let the monitor reach only 200°F. Hold it there for about 1 hour, then let the stove cool to room temperature.
  2. Light a second fire and let the stove reach no more than 400°F, for 1 hour. Let it cool to room temperature.
  3. Light a third fire and gradually bring the stove to a surface temperature of 500°F, and hold it there. Let it cool to room temperature. Break-in is done.
Running too hot? Keep the surface under 400°F on every break-in fire except the last. If it goes over, slide the air lever all the way left. The stove top may keep climbing until the wood burns down a little; that's normal. Never pull burning logs out to cool it.

Odor and smoke at first

A new painted stove normally gives off some odor and smoke during its first fires while the high-temperature paint and materials cure. Open a window or door for extra fresh air.

air.title: Air control & the combustor monitor
air.html:
The primary air lever is at the front center of the stove, just below the door. Slide it right for more air and a hotter, faster fire; slide it left for less air and a longer, lower burn. Air to the catalyst is set automatically.

LowFully to the left · blower minimum
Medium low1/4" to the right · blower minimum
Medium high3/8" to the right · blower medium
HighFully to the right · blower high

Blower speeds apply if your stove has the blower kit. The low end is set at the factory, and it's against federal regulations to alter it.

Read the combustor monitor

The thermometer in the right side reads the heat just behind the catalyst. Keep the lever fully right at least until it reads 500°F, hold that for 15-20 minutes, then turn down to the medium low to medium high range. The cleanest burn is between 500°F and 800°. When it's working you'll see jets of flame at the baffle ports, a red-glowing catalyst, and little or no chimney smoke.

Note: p. 10 says to keep the air fully open for the first five minutes of the Low, Medium Low and Medium High burn rates; p. 11 says to keep it fully open until the monitor reads 500°F, then 15-20 minutes more.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
Reload while there's still a bed of hot embers.

  1. Wear gloves.
  2. Push the air lever fully open (far right).
  3. Open the door slightly first, then fully. This lets the airflow settle so smoke doesn't spill out.
  4. With a stove tool or poker, spread the hot embers evenly around the firebox, away from the air inlets at the front center of the floor.
  5. Load the wood, usually smaller logs first.
  6. Close the door and latch it tightly.
  7. Wait 5 to 10 minutes, then set the air lever for the heat you want. With an ember bed at least 2" thick, you may be able to set it right after closing the door.
Don't overload it. For safety and the best look, stick to a traditional three-log load, and keep logs off the glass so air can move freely.
Empty the ash drawer only before reloading, when the fire is low or out, and close the ash door again right away.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
This stove is listed to burn solid wood only. Dry, seasoned hardwood burns cleaner and more efficiently than softwood or green, freshly cut wood.

  • Seasoning: wood air-dried for 6 to 14 months gives the cleanest, most efficient heat. Wood seasoned more than 2 years burns too quickly.
  • Check it: a seasoned log has many cracks across its ends and is lighter than a fresh one. A moisture meter with probes (from your dealer or a hardware store) should read between 12 and 20%.
  • Wet wood spends its heat driving out water, and that moisture condenses as creosote in the chimney.

Never burn

Coal, garbage, synthetic fuel or logs, anything containing rubber or plastic, petroleum or asphalt products, paints, thinners or solvents, asbestos, construction or demolition debris, railroad ties or pressure-treated wood, manure or animal remains, lawn clippings or yard waste, salt-water driftwood, unseasoned wood, colored paper, paper products, junk mail, cardboard, plywood or particle board.

Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting. Burning anything on the list can release toxic fumes, cause smoke, or permanently ruin the catalytic combustor.

ash.title: Emptying the ashes
ash.html:
The ash pan lets you remove ash without opening the front door. Its door is under the front ash lip: turn the handle counterclockwise to unlatch it and clockwise to latch it.

  1. Empty the pan only before reloading, when the fire is low or out.
  2. Wear stove gloves to handle the ash pan.
  3. Keep the ash door open only long enough to empty the drawer, and close it before you carry the ashes away.
  4. Put the ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set it on a noncombustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn.
  5. If you'll bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until every cinder has cooled completely.
Leave a one-inch bed of ash on the firebox floor; it helps keep a charcoal bed and insulates the bottom. Only use a vacuum made for ashes. Check the ash pan door gasket regularly.
Never run the stove with the ash door open. It leads to over-firing and can damage the stove and the combustor, and that damage isn't covered by the warranty.

glass.title: Glass, gaskets & enamel
glass.html:
The air wash and normal high temperatures keep heavy deposits off the glass, but now and then you'll need to clean off carbon and fly ash. Left too long, they can etch the glass and make it cloudy.

  • Use only an ammonia-free, non-abrasive stove glass cleaner.
  • Clean the glass only at room temperature, never hot.

Door seal check

Close and latch the front door on a dollar bill, then slowly pull it. If it comes out easily, the seal is too loose. Try several spots, and repeat on the ash pan door. Universal Wood Stove Gasket Kit #157050 from your dealer replaces all the gaskets.

Enamel finishes

Clean enamel only when it's cold: wipe with a soft damp cloth, then polish with a dry one. Baking soda and vinegar, left on a stain for a minute or two, lifts most stains. Avoid soapy or abrasive cleaners, and keep trivets, kettles and pots off the enamel.

care.title: Chimney & combustor care
care.html:
Chimney

Inspect the chimney and connector at the start of each heating season and every other month during it. Have them cleaned whenever creosote and fly ash build up more than 1/4 inch anywhere. Creosote is highly flammable, and slow fires make more of it. Your dealer can refer you to a professional chimney sweep.

Catalytic combustor

Look at it at least three times each heating season: open the front door and shine a flashlight up at the catalyst above the baffle. Sweep fly ash off the cells with a soft brush; a shop vacuum can carefully clear them, but the cells are fragile.

Seems sluggish? Burn at medium to high for two or three hours above 500°F to build a full bed of coals, set the air between medium and medium low, and watch the monitor. If it falls below 500°F, the combustor may need cleaning or replacing. Repeat the test 2-3 times to be sure.

Once a year

Empty out all soot and ash, check the stove inside and out with a utility light for cracks or leaks, and replace any cracked parts.

Starting fires with junk mail or lots of newspaper makes fly ash build up on the combustor faster.

safety.title: Safety & chimney fires
safety.html:
• The stove is extremely hot while it's burning. Keep children, clothing and furniture away, and use a child guard screen for small children.
  • Put smoke and carbon monoxide (CO) detectors in the living area and bedrooms. Test them regularly and change the batteries twice a year. In the stove's room, place the detector as far from the stove as you can.
  • Run the stove only with the doors fully closed and the ash door shut. A partly open door can cause over-firing and draw flame and smoke out.
  • Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids on the fire, and keep them away from the stove.

Over-firing

Do not over-fire the stove. If any part of the stove or chimney connector glows (other than the combustor), you're over-firing: running it hotter than it's built for. That can cause a house fire or serious damage, and the warranty doesn't cover it.

The combustor's maximum recommended operating temperature is 1600°F (870°C). It can be damaged if it goes above 1750°F (954°C), even for brief periods of time.

Chimney fire

You'll hear a roaring noise and crackling as burning creosote breaks loose. Close the air lever and make sure the door is shut. Call the fire department and get everyone out. Don't try to put out the fire in the stove or open the door to check on it afterward. Don't use the stove again until the chimney and connector are cleaned and inspected.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul North America warrants these parts to the original retail purchaser, from the date of purchase, against defects in material and workmanship:

Baffle and air manifold partsLimited lifetime, parts only
Cast iron and steel parts5 years
Enamel finish (peeling, fading)2 years
Blowers, thermostatic switches, combustion monitor1 year
High Flow catalytic combustor10 years

A second combustor failure within the 10 years is covered at 50% off current retail. Normal wear and maintenance parts aren't covered: paint, gaskets, burn plates, firebricks, fire grates and glass (glass only against thermal breakage).

What voids or limits it

  • Installation or service by anyone but an authorized installer or service agency, or not following the manual and local codes
  • Over-firing, misuse, or burning with the ash door open
  • Burning improper materials (voids the combustor warranty)

Keep your dated receipt; the serial number is on the label on the back of the stove. Jøtul must hear about a possible defect within 60 days of finding it, so contact your dealer promptly.

Note: p. 28 gives baffle and air manifold parts a lifetime warranty, but also lists baffles and air manifolds among the normal wear parts the warranty doesn't cover.

specOutput.title: Heat output & fuel
specOutput.html:
Heat output range13,200 to 37,000 BTU/hr. (3.9-10.8 kW)
Max. heat output70,000 BTU/hr.
Maker's website: Max Output (kW) 70000.
Heating capacityUp to 2300 sq. ft.
Maximum burn timeUp to 12 hours
Maker's website: Burn time 10 h.
FuelUp to 24" logs (609 mm), solid wood only

The range comes from EPA emissions tests; the maximum reflects a more frequent re-fueling cycle than the EPA High Heat Output test. Capacity and burn time vary with home design, climate, wood type and operation.

The manual also prints 13,000 to 37,000 Btu/hr on p. 2; its Combustion Specifications on p. 3 give 13,200 to 37,000 BTU/hr.

specEff.title: Efficiency & emissions
specEff.html:
EPA efficiency (HHV)78.40%
EPA efficiency (LHV)84.73%
Particulate emissions.50 g/hr. (EPA Test Method 28-R)
CO emissions.50 g/min. (CSA B415.1-10)

Efficiencies per CSA B415.1-10. Meets the 2020 U.S. EPA emission limits. Secondary air is metered automatically by a bimetal coil at the rear inlet and delivered to the baffle and catalytic combustor. Combustor maximum recommended operating temperature 1600°F (870°C); damage can occur above 1750°F (954°C) even briefly.

Maker's website: Combustion technology (from product description): non-catalytic design plus Jøtul High Flow™ Combustor; no bypass.

Listed to ANSI/UL 1482 (U.S.) and ANSI CAN/ULC-628 and CAN/ULC S627 (Canada); safety tests by Intertek Testing Services, Middleton, WI.

specConn.title: Chimney connector
specConn.html:
Diameter6" (152mm), single wall
MaterialBlack steel, 24 gauge minimum
Max. horizontal run36" (915mm)
Recommended total lengthNot over 10 feet
ElbowsNo more than two 90°

No aluminum or galvanized pipe. Crimped (male) end toward the stove; three sheet metal screws per joint; 2 self-drilling screws to the flue collar. Never through an attic, roof space, closet, concealed space, floor or ceiling; all sections accessible for cleaning.

The flue collar ships in the top position and converts to rear exit. Rear exit flue collar height: 28 1/4" (718 mm) with standard legs, 26" (660 mm) with short legs.

specChimney.title: Chimney
specChimney.html:
Approved for a code-approved masonry chimney with flue liner, or a prefabricated chimney meeting UL 103 Type HT (2100°F). An existing chimney must pass a UL 1482 Level II inspection by a qualified technician or building official.

Min. height15 feet (4.57 m)
Above roof3 feet over the roof penetration; 2 feet over anything within 10 feet
Flue areaNot less than the flue collar; no more than three times (interior) or two times (exterior walls)
Fireclay liner8" X 8" nominal, not larger than 8" X 12"; round 6" to 8" ID
Draft.05 - .10 w.c. (p. 11)

Liner at least 5/8" thick in refractory mortar, 1/4" air space to the chimney wall; brick or block 4" nominal, rubble stone 12". No other appliance on the flue; airtight clean-out at the base. Prefab: maker's clearances, usually a minimum of 2". Excessive draft can be corrected with a butterfly damper.

The minimum chimney height is 15 feet (4.57 m); p. 5 also notes that chimneys shorter than 14 feet may not provide adequate draft, which can spill smoke into the room when loading or with the door open.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
From Intertek testing with the chimney connection in the system. Unprotected walls, side / rear / corner:

Single wall pipe, no heatshields14" / 18" / 13"
Single wall pipe w/ rear heatshield14" / 10" / 9"
Rear heatshield + connector shield14" / 6" / 9"
Double wall pipe w/ rear heatshield14" / 6" / 9"

Walls protected per NFPA 211 or CAN/CSA-B365-M93: 6" / 12" / 9" with single wall pipe and no heatshields; 6" / 10" / 9" with the rear heatshield; 6" / 6" / 6" with a connector shield or double wall pipe.

Left side load door to combustibles36" min. (p. 23)

No heat shield other than Rear Heatshield Kit #154332 may be used; it doesn't affect side clearances. The left side load door must be locked in alcove and corner installations. The corner-to-floor-protection and floor protection width dimensions (US and CAN differ) are lettered on the table and diagrams on pp. 22-23; read them from the manual.

specMantel.title: Connector & mantel clearances
specMantel.html:
Horizontal connector clearance (X), from NFPA 211 and independent of stove position:

Single-wall pipe18" unprotected · 12" protected
Double-wall pipe6" unprotected · 6" protected

Fireplace mantel and trim

Stove side to side trim (1" thick or less)12"
Stove top to upper trim (1" thick or less)16"
Stove top to mantel (12" maximum depth)30"

Mantel and trim clearances may be reduced by 50% using the protection methods in NFPA 211 or similar local regulations.

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
Required in any installation unless on concrete over earth. The supplied bottom heat shield must be installed. Use continuous non-combustible material, sections mortared or sealed together, carpet removed underneath.

US16 in. forward of the door opening, 8 in. from its sides, 2 in. under the connector: 50.25" wide x 40.75" deep min.
Canada18" from the front, 8 in. sides and rear, 2 in. under the connector: 52.25" wide x 48.75" deep
Maker's website: Minimum hearth 54.5 x 50.5. Install to the manual.
Alternate hearth42.25" wide x 40.75" (US) / 48.75" (Can) deep, only with the left side door locked
AlcovesAdd material with a minimum R-value of 1.6

Vinyl and similar flooring may be damaged within 57" of the front of the stove; Jøtul recommends no luxury vinyl flooring in that space. Appendix B (p. 27) shows how to qualify alternate floor materials by R-value.

specAlcove.title: Alcove & mobile home
specAlcove.html:
Alcove (figs. 9 and 10, p. 17)

  • Listed double-wall pipe; bottom heatshield in all alcoves; Rear Heat Shield #154332 in an unprotected alcove.
  • Protected alcove: side and rear walls protected per NFPA 211, 1" off the floor and at least 1" off the wall; height including the bottom air space 48".
  • Hearth: UL/ULC listed Type II thermal floor protector, or material with a minimum R value of 1.6.
  • Minimum ceiling height off the stove top: 41" (1041 mm) unprotected, 15" (380mm) protected.
  • Left side load door prohibited: install Side Door Lock Kit #155850.
The manual also prints this kit number once as 155840 (p. 8); pp. 7, 8, 15, 17, 22 and 23 give #155850.

Mobile home

  • Secure the stove to the floor with Floor Mounting Kit #750304; keep the structure intact.
  • Chimney attached directly to the stove, at least 3 ft. above the roof and 2 ft. above any part of the home within 10 ft.; termination removable at or below 13.5 ft. without special tools.
  • Spark arrester at the termination: net free area at least four times the chimney outlet, height at least one-half the flue diameter, openings passing a 3/8" sphere but not one over 1/2".
  • Outside air required: Outside Air Kit #154335 only (3 inch adapter), duct termination no higher than the stove's air inlet.
  • Do not install the stove in a bedroom or sleeping area.
Note: p. 8 says all mobile-home chimney components must comply with UL 103 "Standard for 650°C Factory-built Chimneys"; p. 4 requires UL 103 Type HT (2100°F) prefabricated chimneys.

conflicts.issue: Heat output range low end: 13,000 to 37,000 Btu/hr on p. 2 vs 13,200 to 37,000 BTU/hr. in the Combustion Specifications on p. 3 (catalog uses 13,200).
Side Door Lock Kit part number: 155840 once in the alcove section on p. 8; #155850 on pp. 7, 8, 15, 17, 22 and 23. Also shown in step7.
Minimum chimney height 15 feet (4.57 m) vs 'Chimneys shorter than 14 feet may not provide adequate draft', both p. 5. Also shown in step3.
conflicts.reason: p. 5 sets the minimum chimney height at 15 feet (4.57 m); the line that chimneys shorter than 14 feet may not provide adequate draft is a draft warning, not a second minimum. A chimney that meets the 15-foot minimum satisfies both, so the guide states both plainly (step3, specChimney).

conflicts.issue: How long to keep the primary air fully open: 'Full Open (Right) for the first five minutes of the Low, Medium Low and Medium High burn rate' (p. 10) vs 'at least until the monitor registers 500°F... maintain that temperature for 15-20 minutes before adjusting' (p. 11).

Grate: safety notice 'DO NOT USE A GRATE OR ELEVATE THE FIRE. BUILD THE FIRE DIRECTLY ON THE HEARTH' (p. 3) vs 'Burn only solid wood directly on the bottom grate of the stove' and newspaper 'directly on the grate' (p. 11); the parts list includes Grate, F 500 V3 105015 (p. 21).
Section A gives baffle and air manifold components a limited lifetime warranty (parts only), but exclusion 1 lists baffles and air manifolds among normal wear-and-tear parts not covered; both p. 28.

Mobile-home chimney components must comply with 'UL 103 Standard for 650°C Factory-built Chimneys' (p. 8), while the general requirement is a UL 103 Type HT (2100°F) prefabricated chimney (p. 4; HT also p. 5).

review.notes: Single manual (139946-22, July 2025), installation and operation combined; all pagerefs are physical pages of doc 1 (printed folios match). Catalog values that match the manual: 13,200-37,000 BTU/hr output (p. 3; p. 2 says 13,000, flagged), 70,000 max output, 2300 sq. ft., HHV 78.4% (pp. 3, 9), .50 g/hr particulate, 24" logs, 6" connector, catalytic, EPA 2020, outside air kit, blower kit, mobile home approval. The manual does not state firebox volume, weight, or overall height/width/depth; Fig. 1b (p. 16) shows a 24 3/4" (629mm) dimension only on a drawing, so catalog firebox_cu_ft, weight_lb, height_in, width_in and depth_in were not checked. Clearances: the side/rear/corner values were read from the p. 22 text table (letter codes are consistent across rows: A=14", B=18", C=13", F=12", G=6", H=9", J=10"). The corner-to-front-floor-protection and front floor protection width values (D/E/I/K: US 65 1/2", 59 7/8", 55 5/8", 34 1/8"; CAN 67 1/2", 61 7/8", 57 5/8", 44 1/4") and the p. 23 diagram numbers (e.g. HEARTH EXT US 34 1/4"/30 1/4"/27 1/4", CAN 32"/28"/25") were not transcribed: they don't line up with each other (E is 34 1/8" US / 44 1/4" CAN on p. 22 but HEARTH EXT 34 1/4" US / 32" CAN on p. 23) or obviously with the p. 7 floor protector sizes. Reviewer should check the PDF drawings. Fig. 10 (p. 17) alcove dimensions (48" Max., 40.5" Min., 12", 6") are drawing-only and were not transcribed; p. 17 also has a line of garbled characters in the Fig. 9 area that does not decode with the 29-code-point rule, left out. No French-only text; the cover only notes a French manual is available. The monitor install text cites figs. 13c-13e on 'pg. 18'; those figures are on physical p. 19. 'DO NOT INSTALL THE STOVE IN A BEDROOM OR SLEEPING AREA' sits in the mobile home section (p. 8) and is presented there. No troubleshooting chart: fault panels are built from the manual's draft (pp. 3-5), over-firing (pp. 12-13, 28) and combustor test (pp. 9, 24) text. No error codes. Blower Kit 156431 is covered only in Accessories (p. 15) and the blower-speed column of the control table (p. 10), so it has no tile of its own. Parts list (p. 21) gives 118070 for both #32 Coiled Spring Pin and #45 Set Screw M6x25; not used in the guide. The combustor maintenance video link on p. 24 is omitted (no links in drawers).
